info.title: Transpareo API
info.description:
This site runs on the [Transpareo](https://transpareo.com) product information platform. The REST API gives programs access to products, product components, brands, Digital Product Passports, categories and configuration. The version is selected with the `Accept` header, not a path segment.

The guide at [/apidocs/guide](/apidocs/guide) is the narrative companion to this reference: credentials, permissions, pagination, idempotency, the passport flows, the event feed, webhooks, rate limits and the error format. It is also served as Markdown at [/apidocs/guide.md](/apidocs/guide.md).

Programs authenticate with the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant. Exchange the client id and secret once, then send the token on every request:

```
curl -X POST https://<host>/api/oauth/token -d grant_type=client_credentials -d client_id=<key> -d client_secret=<secret>

curl https://<host>/api/me -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>"
```

oauth2.description:
OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant for API consumers. The consumer's key is the client id and its secret the client secret. Exchange them at the token endpoint, as form fields or as HTTP Basic credentials, and send the returned token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

A token lives one hour and is bound to the host that issued it. `scope` narrows a token to a subset of the consumer's permission keys; without it the token carries all of them.

scopes.brand_access: Read brands and write own brands
scopes.component_access: Read components and write own components
scopes.export_access: Start, poll and download passport exports
scopes.import_access: Upload, map, validate, execute and revert imports
scopes.product_access: Read products and write own products
scopes.product_category_access: Read product categories and write own categories
scopes.brand_write: Write every brand of the workspace
scopes.component_write: Write every component of the workspace
scopes.dpp_dynamic: Update the dynamic data of passports
scopes.dpp_history: Read the events and versions of passports

userToken.description:
User JWT token obtained from `POST /session`.

Format: `Bearer <jwt_token>` (the older `UR <jwt_token>` prefix is still accepted)

API-Count.description: Number of records in this response

Link.description: `<url>; rel="next"` while a further page exists

Idempotent-Replayed.description: Present when the response is the stored answer of an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key

idempotency_key.name: Idempotency-Key
idempotency_key.description: Makes the request safe to repeat. The same key and body within 24 hours replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with another body answers 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; a key whose first request is still running answers 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`.

Forbidden.description: Not authorized to perform this action

example.message: You are not authorized to perform this action

AsyncTask.description: The polling payload of an asynchronous bulk create. While the task runs, only `taskId`, `status` and `progress` are present; the counts and the error detail appear once it completes. Successful rows are counted, not listed - only rejected rows carry detail, so an integrator can patch and resubmit that subset.

progress.description: Percent of rows processed. Capped at 99 until the task completes.

createdCount.description: Rows that wrote a passport and published its first version

duplicateCount.description: Rows whose natural key already mapped to a published passport

errors.description: The rejected rows, each carrying its 1-based `row` number alongside the row outcome. Capped at 1000 entries.

row.description: 1-based position of the row in the submitted body

published.description: Follows from the brand's products; a brand with accessible products is published

permalink.description: Only present for published brands when lists are enabled

productsCount.description: Only present for published brands when lists are enabled

name.description: The brand name, harmonised the way the application manager does it

BulkRow.description: One line of the NDJSON response to a synchronous bulk create. `status` discriminates the three outcomes: `created` (a passport was written and its first version published), `duplicate` (the row's natural key already maps to a published passport, which is returned unchanged) and `error` (the row was rejected or its publish failed). Rows come back in completion order, not input order - correlate them by `serialIdentifier` / `batchIdentifier` / `modelIdentifier`, which every outcome echoes.

id.description: Passport id. On `created` and `duplicate`, and on an `error` whose passport row was written but whose publish failed.

code.description: The public passport code printed on QR codes. Present alongside `id`.

error.description: On `error` only: `DPP_INVALID_LINE` (the line is not a JSON object), `DPP_INVALID` (the passport failed validation, see `fields`) or `DPP_PUBLISH_FAILED` (the passport row was kept unpublished; resubmit the same row to resume it).

fields.description: On `DPP_INVALID`: the failing attribute names mapped to their error.

BulkValidateRow.description: One line of the NDJSON response to a bulk dry run. `status` discriminates the four outcomes: `valid` (the row would be created and published), `invalid` (the row carries model errors, see `fields`), `duplicate` (the row's natural key already maps to a published passport, which is echoed unchanged) and `error` (the line could not be read). Results come back in input order and `row` numbers them from one, so no identifier is needed to correlate them.

row.description: Position of the input row, counted from one

fields.description: On `valid` and `invalid`: the model errors of the row, one entry per attribute, empty on `valid`.

validation.description: The report a publish of this row would produce. Absent when model errors stopped the row before the publish rules ran.

id.description: On `duplicate`: the id of the passport the natural key maps to.

code.description: On `duplicate`: the public passport code printed on QR codes.

modelIdentifier.description: On `duplicate`: echoed from the passport the row maps to.

error.description: On `error` only: the line is not a JSON object.

Category.description: Hierarchical category node (used for product categories, component functions, types, and property categories)

categories.description: Child categories (recursive, only present when children exist)

publishedAt.description: Present only when the component is published

ComponentDetail.description: Full component details (returned by show action)

publishedAt.description: Present only when the component is published

rating.description: Component rating (very_good/good/neutral/bad/very_bad) when unlocked via DPP key or authorized. Returns 'protected' otherwise. Only present when ratings are enabled.

properties.description: Component properties grouped by type name. Only present in show action. Protected types return {"protected": true} instead of values when user is not unlocked.

rated.description: Whether this property type contributes to rating

protected.description: Whether this property type is protected (requires login)

citations.description: Scientific citations. Only present when citations are enabled in tenant config and the user has access (citations may be protected behind login).

mediafiles.description: Component images. Only present in show action.

products.description: Sample products containing this component. Only present when lists are enabled in tenant config.

ComponentInput.description: A component write. `component` carries the attributes; `properties` and `templateIds` ride beside it in the shape the application manager's form sends and are applied after the component is saved.

properties.description: Property changes keyed by property type id. Values are matched against existing properties of that type, so two components naming the same value share one property.

new.description: Values to add, per property type id

points.description: The rating points of the value, where the type is rated

existing.description: Properties to change, per property type id, keyed by property id. An empty value leaves the property as it is.

templateIds.description: The components this one inherits properties from; replaces the current set

Config.description: Full tenant configuration including feature flags, languages, navigation, and localization

ratings.description: Rating definitions (only when ratings are enabled)

currencies.description: Available currencies (only when memberships are enabled)

ConsumerIdentity.description: The API consumer behind a bearer token and what that token allows

key.description: The consumer's key (the OAuth client id)

authority.description: True for a regulator consumer issued by the platform

permissions.description: Every permission key the consumer holds

scope.description: The permission keys this token carries, among those the consumer still holds

resourceScope.description: Record ids per model class the consumer is confined to; empty means the whole workspace

Dpp.description: Digital Product Passport with QR code and linked product

url.description: Full URL that the QR code resolves to

granularity.description: Which unit the passport stands for

modelIdentifier.description: Only present when set. Inherited from the product when the create named none.

batchIdentifier.description: Only present when set. Carried at batch and item granularity.

serialIdentifier.description: Only present when set. Carried at item granularity.

passportStatus.description: The EN 18223 status of a carrier taken out of circulation. Only present once the passport is voided or superseded.

voidedAt.description: When the passport was voided. Only present on a voided passport.

voidedReason.description: Why the passport was voided. Only present on a voided passport.

supersededBy.description: The code of the passport that replaced this one. Only present on a superseded passport.

pdfUrl.description: URL to download QR code as PDF

pngUrl.description: URL to download QR code as PNG

propertyTypes.description: Property types selected for display on the DPP page (only when configured)

dppComponents.description: Linked product's components with ratings (only present when the product has components)

dppProperties.description: Public product properties grouped for display (only present when configured)

validation.description: The report a publish of the passport as it stands would produce, the same one the dry run answers with. Present on the create and update responses only, and null there when the passport failed model validation.

publishBlocked.description: Whether a publish of the passport as it stands would be refused. Present on the create and update responses only.

DppBulkRowInput.description: One row of a bulk passport body. Read the same way by the bulk create and the bulk dry run, so a batch that validates is the batch that will be created.

unlockableId.description: Id of the product this passport describes

locale.description: Falls back to the request's language

granularity.description: Which unit the passport stands for, and therefore which natural key deduplicates the row

batchIdentifier.description: Bound to a batch of the product, created on first use

DppEvent.description: One entry of a passport's event log. Versioned types ride a registered DppVersion and carry `dppVersionNumber`; local types are recorded in the passport's own log and carry none.

eventType.description: Versioned types (`published` ... `corrected`) ride a registered version; local types (`inspection` ... `validation_warning`) do not.

statusFrom.description: The passport status before the transition. Only on `status_change` events.

statusTo.description: The passport status after the transition. Only on `status_change` events.

actorType.description: The class of the actor that recorded the event, `User` or `ApiConsumer`.

actorLabel.description: Denormalised actor name, kept readable after the actor row is gone

data.description: Free-form metadata the caller attached to the event

dppVersionNumber.description: The version this event was sealed into. Absent on a local event and on a pending draft.

DppEventInput.description: The event to append. `eventType` decides the branch - `status_change` drives a status transition and requires `status`; every other type records a plain event. The versioned types are not accepted here, they ride their own operations.

eventType.description: `status_change` drives the transition and is recorded as an event of type `lifecycle_transition`; every other value is recorded verbatim. A versioned type answers 422 `EVENT_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED` - those ride the void / supersede / reissue / publish operations instead.

status.description: The status to move to. Required on `status_change`, ignored otherwise.

gln.description: GS1 Global Location Number of the place the event happened. Falls back to the calling consumer's GLN, then to the workspace GLN.

publish.description: Seals the event into the Vault (and, for a status change, into a new registered version) instead of leaving it as a pending draft. Honours the publish-debounce window.

data.description: Free-form metadata carried onto the event

unlockableType.description: Type of linked record (defaults to Product)

granularity.description: Which unit the passport stands for, and therefore which identifiers it needs

modelIdentifier.description: Falls back to what the product supplies - its GTIN, else its manufacturer part number

batchIdentifier.description: Required at batch and item granularity. The lot is created from the product as it stands the first time its identifier is used, and reused by every later passport of the same lot.

dynamicData.description: Values that change over the unit's life, keyed by the vocabulary term of their property type. They ride on the separately signed dynamic surface and never enter a signed per-version snapshot; `PATCH /dpps/{id}/dynamic_data` writes them afterwards.

propertyTypeIds.description: Property type IDs to display on the DPP page

DppRequirements.description: What a passport of one product needs at one granularity, and what the product still lacks, before anything is written. Field names throughout are the wire names, so a program copies them into a create or a bulk row as they are.

product.description: The product a passport would describe

modelIdentifier.description: The model identifier the product supplies on its own - its GTIN, else its manufacturer part number. A row that names one of its own wins over it.

defaultGranularity.description: The granularity a create gets when its body names none

granularities.description: The identifiers each granularity keys on, keyed by granularity, so a client can offer the choice without a second request

identifiers.description: What the requested granularity needs. The model identifier comes from the product; the lot and serial identifiers are the caller's.

value.description: The value the product supplies, when it has one

batch.description: The lot a batch or item passport freezes from. Null at model granularity, which has no lot.

dynamicPropertyTypes.description: Property types whose value changes over a unit's life. Their values ride on the separately signed dynamic surface, keyed by the vocabulary term in `namespace`, and never enter a signed per-version snapshot.

namespace.description: The vocabulary term the value is written under

inheritedProperties.description: The product properties a passport of this product inherits, with the values the product carries today

outlook.description: The report a publish of a model passport of this product would produce right now, so the product is completed before a passport is written rather than at publish. Same `must` and `should` entries as `DppValidationReport`, without the validator version.

templates.description: Bodies ready to fill, with the blanks the caller supplies left empty

batch.description: A lot is created from the product as it stands the first time its identifier is used; later passports of the same lot reuse it.

DppValidationFailure.description: One rule the passport does not satisfy, as the validator recorded it.

path.description: Where the rule applies, dotted from the credential subject of the snapshot

field.description: The label a person sees for that path, in the tenant's language

constraint.description: The rule that failed. A snapshot rule reports its constraint - `min_count`, `max_count`, `min_length`, `max_length`, `pattern`, `in`, `has_value` or `datatype`. A rule the linked product itself failed reports the model error name instead, for example `invalid` or `blank`.

example.message: issuer.name requires at least 1 value(s), got 0

DppValidationOutcome.description: The answer of the dry run behind `POST /dpps/validate`: whether the payload would be accepted, the model errors it carries, and the report a publish would produce. Nothing is written either way, so `valid: false` is the normal answer for an unacceptable payload rather than a failed request.

valid.description: True when the payload carries no model error and no rule blocks its publish

fields.description: The model errors of the payload, one entry per attribute, empty when there are none. Same shape as the `fields` of a 422.

validation.description: Null while `fields` is not empty - a payload that cannot be saved is never run against the publish rules.

publishBlocked.description: Whether a publish would be refused, for a model error or for a `must` failure

must.message: issuer.name requires at least 1 value(s), got 0

DppValidationReport.description: The rules a publish of the passport as it stands would apply, split by severity. A `must` failure blocks the publish; a `should` failure is recorded as a warning and lets it through. Two empty arrays mean the passport publishes cleanly.

validatorVersion.description: The rule set that produced this report

should.description: Recommendations that do not block a publish

must.message: issuer.name requires at least 1 value(s), got 0

DppVersion.description: One registered version of a passport - the signed JSON-LD snapshot published at that point, with the integrity pair a reader verifies it against. Same shape as the entries of the per-passport manifest on the public CDN.

number.description: Version number, 1 for the first published snapshot

hashCanonicalForm.description: The canonicalization the hash was taken over

hashValue.description: Digest of the published snapshot bytes

url.description: Public URL of the signed JSON-LD snapshot

schemaVersion.description: Snapshot schema generation this version was written under

DppVersionSnapshot.description: One published version of a passport, with the signed JSON-LD document as it was served, the hash it was signed over and the address it is kept at.

code.description: The public code of the passport the version belongs to

version.description: The version number that was asked for

hashValue.description: SHA-256 over the signed document, the value a verifier checks

url.description: Where the signed document is served from

DynamicDataInput.description: The keys to write onto the passport's dynamic-data surface. Sent keys are merged into the stored set; a key sent as an explicit null is removed. Field names are yours - no schema is imposed until the EU Battery Regulation's implementing acts pin the list.

hint.description: What to do next, present when the platform has advice for this code (for example which permission a 403 needs, or where to get a new token)

docsUrl.description: The section of the API guide that explains this refusal, as an absolute URL on the host that answered. Present on every error.

fields.description: Present on validation failures, one entry per attribute. An entry carries whatever the validation recorded besides its message, so a caller can act on it without parsing prose.

field.description: On a publish refused by a validation rule, the label a person would look for. The entry is keyed by the failing path rather than by an attribute there.

missing.description: On a product refused for missing mandatory properties, the names of the property types still needed

EventFeed.description: One page of the workspace-wide event feed. Each entry is a `DppEvent` with the id that serves as cursor and the passport it belongs to.

id.description: The event id, also the cursor that continues after it

dppId.description: Id of the passport the event belongs to

dppCode.description: Public code of that passport, absent once the passport row is gone

nextCursor.description: Pass as `since` on the next call. Null only before the first event exists.

Export.description: One export and where it stands. The archive fields appear once `status` is `completed`; `failure` once it is `failed`.

code.description: The short code the application manager lists the export under

progress.description: Percent of the work done. 100 once completed.

failure.description: Why the export failed. Only on `failed`.

recordCount.description: Passports, products and components exported. On `completed`.

expiresAt.description: When the archive is deleted, seven days after completion. On `completed`.

downloadUrl.description: Where to fetch the archive. On `completed`.

ExportInput.description: What to export and how. Every field is optional; the default is the whole passport catalogue as JSON-LD.

dataType.description: The API exports passports. Payments, users and audit logs are exported from the application manager.

format.description: `jsonld` packs one document per passport, product and component into a tar archive; the tabular formats flatten the catalogue into one sheet each

normalize.description: Resolve references into the exported rows instead of carrying ids

includeMedia.description: Copy the product and component media files into the archive

Grant.description: The client credentials of the short-lived child consumer the grant issued. Exchange them at the token endpoint exactly like your own, then write events against the one passport named in `scope`. The secret is shown once, in this response, and never again.

key.description: The child consumer's key (its OAuth client id)

secret.description: The child consumer's secret. Returned only here.

expiresAt.description: When the child consumer stops working, 24 hours after issue

scope.description: The single passport the child may act on

GrantInput.description: How to name the passport the grant is scoped to. Either send the scanned `dppCode`, or resolve it from GS1 identifiers - `gtin` alone finds the model passport, plus `batch` for the batch passport and plus `serial` for the item passport. A non-string value is ignored, so no query operator can travel in.

dppCode.description: The public passport code printed on the QR code

gtin.description: GTIN of the product, in any of the GS1 lengths

batch.description: Batch identifier. Narrows the GTIN lookup to that batch; without `serial` it selects the batch passport.

serial.description: Serial identifier. Narrows the GTIN lookup to a single item passport.

Import.description: One import and where it stands. `preview` is present while the import is `fresh`; `progress` while a task runs; `errorGroups` and `rowErrors` once a validation or a run has found problems.

status.description: `fresh` waits for a mapping, `mapped` may be validated or executed, `validated` carries the dry run's findings, `importing` and `restoring` have a task running, `completed`, `failed` and `reverted` are final

mappings.description: The stored mapping, one action per column, in the shape of `ImportMappingsInput`

options.description: The options the run reads, `published` and `skipBackup`

errorGroups.description: The problems the validation or the run found, grouped by cause, each with the count and up to five sample rows

rowErrors.description: One entry per failing row, so the rows can be patched and sent again. Capped at 1000 entries. Each phase replaces the entries of the one before, so they describe the phase that ran last, and `errorGroups` says the same thing grouped by cause.

row.description: The row as the file counts it, from one

code.description: What kind of failure it was, such as `mapping_failed`, `save_failed` or `validation_name`

field.description: The attribute the failure names, where it names one

revertable.description: A completed or failed run with a backup or created records can be reverted

progress.description: Percent of the running task, while one runs

ImportMappingsInput.description: One action per column of the upload, keyed by the column as the preview names it, plus the options a run reads. Every required attribute of the data type must be covered by a column mapped to it, unless the rows carry it on their own, as a JSON upload does with `name`.

action.description: `map_to_attribute` feeds a core attribute, `use_existing` a property type by id, `create_new` a property type by name (this changes the schema of the workspace for good and is never inferred), `skip` drops the column

typeId.description: With `use_existing`, the id of one of the preview's `propertyTypes`

typeName.description: With `create_new`, the name of the property type to create

isSingleValue.description: Whether the column holds one value per row; defaults to what the preview found

published.description: Publish the records the import creates

skipBackup.description: Execute without the backup a revert would restore from

ImportPreview.description: What the upload looks like and what a mapping may target. Present while the import is `fresh`. An agent given this answers `PUT /imports/{id}/mappings` in one turn.

header.description: The column header as the file spells it

column.description: The key the mapping is written under

sampleValues.description: Up to three values from the column

singleValue.description: One value per row, or several separated by the value separator

coreAttribute.description: The core attribute the suggestion feeds

typeId.description: The property type the suggestion matched

matchType.description: How the header was recognised. `exact` and `attribute` resolve on their own; `fuzzy` is a guess by similarity; `none` found nothing.

similarity.description: The similarity of a fuzzy match, 0 to 1

coreAttributes.description: The attributes `map_to_attribute` may target for this data type

requiredAttributes.description: The attributes a mapping must cover

propertyTypes.description: The workspace's property types `use_existing` may target

default.description: Whether this is the default language

currencyCode.description: Currency code (when not including full currency object)

Leadgen.description: Lead generation campaign with overlay and form

popup.description: Whether the overlay is a popup

example.name: Autumn campaign
example.headline: Register your product
example.body: Two minutes, and the warranty runs for three years.
example.message: Thank you, the registration is in.

url.description: Full URL to the file (includes asset host)

image.description: Whether the file is an image

path.description: URL path (includes locale prefix when locale_in_path is enabled)

OAuthError.description: The error response of RFC 6749, section 5.2

Overlay.description: DPP overlay content displayed on scan

apiKey.description: Public API key for client-side integration

Plan.description: Subscription plan with features and pricing variants

trialDuration.description: Trial period (only shown to users who have not used a trial)

ident.description: Price identifier used in plan selection

PrivateProperties.description: The confidential rows of one passport version, as an ecdsa-sd-2023 derived Verifiable Credential. The Vault holds the full credential; what comes back here is the view this reader is entitled to - the mandatory public statements plus the restricted rows the reader may see. `legitimateInterest` rows survive only while the reader's access-group membership admits them, `onDemand` rows go to any authenticated reader, and `authorities` rows are never served here. The derived proof is the filter, so the response stays verifiable against the issuer keys and no confidential statement is signed away. JSON-LD keys (`@context`, `@type`) pass through unchanged.

@id.description: The credential's own IRI, the passport URL with a `#credential` fragment

credentialSubject.description: The revealed statements, in the shape the passport snapshot uses

proof.description: One derived ecdsa-sd-2023 proof per base proof the credential was issued with

Product.description: Product summary (returned in list endpoints). The `show` action returns ProductDetail with additional nested data.

publishedAt.description: Present only when the product is published

rating.description: Component rating (A-D) when unlocked, or 'protected' when access is restricted. Only present when ratings are enabled.

gtin.description: Global Trade Item Number (only when present)

token.description: Claim token for unclaimed products (only when present)

ProductComponent.description: A component as it appears within a product (includes rating and properties when unlocked)

percentage.description: The share of the product the component makes up. Only present when the product names one.

ProductDetail.description: Full product details (returned by show action and permalink resolution). Includes nested brand, components, properties, categories, and mediafiles.

rating.description: Product rating (very_good/good/neutral/bad/very_bad) when unlocked via DPP key or authorized user. Returns 'protected' when access is restricted. Only present when ratings are enabled in tenant config.

brand.description: Full brand object. Only present in show/permalink actions; list responses return brand_name string instead.

gtin.description: Global Trade Item Number. Only present when the product has a GTIN assigned.

token.description: Claim token for unclaimed products. Only present when the product has an unresolved token.

ownerName.description: Name of the record owner. Only present in show action when the product has an owner.

editable.description: Whether the current user can edit this product. Only present when true.

components.description: Product components with ratings. Only present in show/permalink actions.

componentsIds.description: The ids of the components the product carries. The dashboard answers these in place of the components themselves.

properties.description: Product properties grouped by property type name. Only present in show/permalink actions. Filtered by the show parameter and user group access.

values.description: The values the product carries for this property type; empty on `GET /products/new`

allowedValues.description: The closed set of values a templated property type accepts (battery chemistries, for example). Only present when the type carries one; a value outside the set is refused.

inputLimit.description: Maximum number of values (only when limited)

hideName.description: Whether to hide the property type name in display

namespace.description: The vocabulary term the value is published under in the passport snapshot. Only present on property types anchored to a vocabulary.

unit.description: The physical unit values are given in. Only present on quantitative property types.

dynamic.description: Whether the value changes over a unit's life. A dynamic value rides on the passport's separately signed dynamic surface and never enters a signed per-version snapshot. Only present when true.

mandatoryWhen.description: Narrows `mandatory` to part of the catalog - the type is required only for products whose value of the property type named by `namespace` is in `values`. Only present when the flag is scoped; an unscoped `mandatory` applies to every product.

namespace.description: The vocabulary term of the property type that decides

values.description: The values of that property for which this type is mandatory

hint.description: Explanatory note shown with the field. Only present when the type carries one.

icon.description: Name of the icon shown with the field. Only present when the type carries one.

post.description:
Creates a new Digital Product Passport linked to a product. Generates a unique short code and QR code.

`granularity` says which unit the passport stands for and therefore which identifiers it needs: `model` needs none of its own, `batch` needs a `batchIdentifier`, `item` needs a `serialIdentifier` as well. The lot is created from the product as it stands the first time its identifier is used and reused by every later passport of the same lot.

The answer carries `validation` and `publishBlocked` alongside the passport: the same report `POST /dpps/validate` produces, over the record that was just written, so a caller that skipped the dry run still sees what a publish would refuse or warn about.

201.description: DPP created, carrying `validation` and `publishBlocked` besides the passport

post.description:
The dry run of `POST /dpps`: the same body, answered with the model errors the payload carries and the report a publish would produce, and nothing written. A separate path rather than a flag on the create, so a misspelled option can never mint a signed passport. A batch or item payload is checked against the lot it would freeze from without creating that lot.

A payload the platform would refuse is a plain `200` with `valid: false` - the request succeeded, the passport would not. Only a missing permission, a missing `dpp` object or an unreadable body answer with an error status.

200.description: The outcome of the dry run. Nothing was written.

post.description:
Streams passports in as newline-delimited JSON, one passport per line, so a line of production writes one request instead of thousands. Each row is created and its first version published; the response reports one result line per input row.

An optional first line `{"shared": {...}}` carries batch-wide defaults that each following row deep-merges over (a nested `"__replace__": true` opts a sub-tree out of the merge). An unsupported `shared.granularity` is rejected before any row is processed; per-row problems never abort the batch.

Row keys may be written in camelCase (`unlockableId`, `modelIdentifier`, `serialIdentifier`) or as the snake_case attribute names; `tenantData` is an alias for `dynamicData`. The keys inside `dynamicData` are left as they are.

Resubmission is safe. Rows are deduplicated by natural key rather than by `Idempotency-Key`: at `model` granularity that is `modelIdentifier`, at `batch` it adds `batchIdentifier`, at `item` it adds `serialIdentifier`. A key that already maps to a published passport comes back as `duplicate`; one that maps to a passport that never published is resumed and published, so a retry after a partial failure finishes the job instead of duplicating it.

Synchronous by default, capped at 500 rows and 5 MB. Send `Prefer: respond-async` to have the body persisted and processed by a background task instead: the response is `202` with a polling URL, and the caps rise to 50000 rows and 25 MB. Beyond that, batch across requests.

parameters.name: Prefer
parameters.description: Send `respond-async` to process the batch in the background and answer 202 with a polling URL.

schema.description: Newline-delimited JSON, not a JSON array: one object per line, optionally preceded by a single `{"shared": {...}}` envelope line.

200.description: One result line per input row, in completion order

schema.description: Newline-delimited JSON, not a JSON array: one result object per line.

post.description:
The dry run of `POST /dpps/bulk`: the same newline-delimited JSON in, one result line per input row out, and nothing written. Rows are read exactly as the create reads them - the optional `{"shared": {...}}` envelope, the deep merge, the camelCase aliases - so a batch that validates here is the batch that will be created.

Each row comes back as `valid`, `invalid`, `duplicate` or `error`, numbered from one in input order. No passport, lot or version is written, and the rows do not count against the consumer's bulk item cap, so a batch may be validated as often as it takes to get it right.

Synchronous only, capped at 500 rows and 5 MB like the synchronous create. There is no asynchronous mode; `Prefer: respond-async` has no effect here.

post.summary: Append an event to a DPP
post.description:
Records one event against the passport. `eventType: status_change` moves the passport to the `status` you name and is recorded as a `lifecycle_transition`; any other type is recorded as a plain event.

An event is a pending draft until it is sealed. Send `publish: true` to seal it into the Vault at once (a status change is sealed into a new registered version); leave it out to keep the draft open. At most one pending event exists per passport, so a second call while one is open answers 409 until it is sealed or discarded.

Versioned event types are rejected here: they stand for operations that mint a version, and those have their own endpoints (void, supersede, reissue, publish).

patch.description: Writes high-frequency telemetry (state of health, cycle count, and similar) onto the passport. Dynamic data is mutable state: it is carried on a separately signed surface and never enters a signed per-version snapshot, so a write mints no version and records no lifecycle event. Keys you send are merged into the stored set; a key sent as an explicit null is removed. At most 250 keys per passport and 4096 bytes per value, both measured on the result of the merge - so removing keys in the same request frees room under the cap. Requires the dpp_dynamic permission.

example.message: At most 250 keys and 4096 bytes per value

get.summary: Poll the feed of passport events
get.description:
Every event recorded on any passport of the workspace, in the order the events were created, as a feed to poll instead of a webhook to host. Keep the `nextCursor` of each answer and pass it as `since` on the next call: the answer then holds only what arrived after it. An empty `events` array is normal between polls; the cursor comes back unchanged.

The cursor is the id of the last event answered. `since` also accepts an ISO 8601 time, to start a feed from a moment rather than from the beginning. Events younger than five seconds are held back until the next call, so nothing can appear behind a cursor a client already holds.

Gated behind `dpp_history` like the per-passport log, because the events carry actor identifiers and free-form metadata. A scope-limited partner-grant token only sees the passports of its grant.

Packs the whole passport catalogue into an archive in the background and answers at once with the export and its `statusUrl`. Poll that URL until `status` is `completed`, then fetch the `downloadUrl` it names. The archive is kept for seven days after completion.

The consumer that starts an export is the only one that can read or download it. One export runs at a time per consumer: while one is pending or running, another request answers 409 `EXPORT_IN_PROGRESS` with a hint naming the URL to poll.

get.description: Where the export stands. While it runs, `progress` climbs; once it completes, the archive size, the counts, `expiresAt` and the `downloadUrl` appear. Another consumer's export answers 404.

The archive of a completed export as `application/gzip`. Before completion the answer is 409 `EXPORT_NOT_READY`; a failed export answers 409 `EXPORT_FAILED`; once the archive has been deleted, seven days after completion, the answer is 410 `EXPORT_EXPIRED`.

post.description:
Turns a scanned QR code into credentials that can write to that one passport. A workshop, certifier or recycler registered as a long-lived API consumer with no passports of its own calls this with the code it scanned and gets back the client credentials of a short-lived child consumer, exchanged for a bearer token exactly like its own. The child may act on that single passport for 24 hours; the caller keeps its own workspace-wide standing.

The child inherits only the event-write permissions the caller itself holds, out of `dpp_events`, `dpp_history` and `dpp_dynamic`, so a grant can never widen access. A caller that holds none of them is refused. A caller already confined to a set of passports can only grant one from that set.

Regulator consumers do not use this flow - their access is platform-issued and workspace-wide - and are refused.

post.description:
One multipart request, the shape every upload API has: `curl -F file=@catalogue.xlsx -F dataType=components`. The importer reads xlsx, csv, ods and json. When every column resolves on its own (the canonical headers of the template `GET /imports/example` serves, or a JSON file whose entries carry the canonical keys) the import comes back `mapped`. Otherwise it is `fresh` and the answer carries the `preview` to write the mapping from; send that with `PUT /imports/{id}/mappings`, or along with the file as `mappings`.

The upload is held for a limited time; once it is gone, the run endpoints answer 410 `IMPORT_EXPIRED`.

put.description: One action per column, in the vocabulary the preview lists. Every required attribute must be covered. `create_new` adds a property type to the workspace for good, so the API only creates one when the mapping says so. The import moves to `mapped`.

422.description: A required attribute no column maps to (`IMPORT_MAPPING_INCOMPLETE`, named in `fields.mappings.missing`)

post.description: The dry run over the whole file in the background, writing nothing. Poll the `statusUrl` until `status` is `validated`; the problems found are in `rowErrors`, one entry per failing row, and in `errorGroups` grouped by cause.

410.description: The upload is no longer available (`IMPORT_EXPIRED`)

post.description:
Writes the rows in the background, after a backup a revert can restore from unless `options.skipBackup` is set. Poll the `statusUrl` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`.

Besides `import_access` this needs the write permission of the data type: `component_write` for components, `product_access` for products, `dpp_bulk_write` for passports. The rows count against the consumer's bulk item cap for the minute.

403.description: Missing `import_access`, or the write permission of the data type (`IMPORT_FORBIDDEN`, the hint names it)

409.description: The import is not mapped, or already running (`IMPORT_NOT_READY`)

410.description: The upload is no longer available (`IMPORT_EXPIRED`)

429.description: The rows exceed the consumer's bulk item cap for this minute (`IMPORT_RATE_LIMITED`, `Retry-After` is set)

post.description: Restores the backup and removes the records the run created, in the background. Refused when records changed since the backup was taken, since restoring would overwrite those changes; `options.force` reverts anyway.

409.description: Nothing to revert (`IMPORT_NOT_REVERTABLE`), or records changed since the backup (`IMPORT_REVERT_STALE`)

post.summary: Exchange client credentials for a bearer token
post.description:
The OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant (RFC 6749, section 4.4). The consumer's key is the client id and its secret the client secret; send them as form fields or as HTTP Basic credentials. The token lives one hour and is bound to this host. `scope` narrows it to a subset of the consumer's permission keys.

Errors use the codes RFC 6749 defines: `invalid_request` (400), `unsupported_grant_type` (400), `invalid_scope` (400), `invalid_client` (401, also for a suspended or expired consumer), plus `access_denied` (403) for an address outside the consumer's allow-list and `slow_down` (429) for a consumer over its hourly rate limit. The exchange is throttled to 10 per minute per address and per client id.

client_id.description: The consumer's key. Omit when sent as HTTP Basic credentials.

client_secret.description: The consumer's secret. Omit when sent as HTTP Basic credentials.

scope.description: Space-separated permission keys to narrow the token to; all granted keys when omitted.

400.description: Malformed request, unsupported grant type or a scope the consumer was not granted

401.description: Unknown client id, wrong secret, or a suspended or expired consumer

403.description: The request address is outside the consumer's IP allow-list

429.description: The consumer is over its hourly rate limit (`Retry-After` is set)

get.description: The consumer behind the bearer token, its permissions, the token's scope and expiry, the consumer's resource scope and rate limit. The cheapest way to check that a credential works. Never returns the secret. A user token gets the consumer error; users read themselves at `GET /users/me`.

get.description:
Returns the properties structure needed for the product creation form: every property type a product of this tenant can carry, keyed by name.

Each entry says what the type needs. `mandatory` marks a value a product cannot go without, and `mandatoryWhen` narrows that to part of the catalog - the type is required only for products whose value of the named property is in its list. `namespace` is the vocabulary term the value is published under, `unit` the physical unit it is given in, and `values` the closed set to choose from where the type has one. `dynamic` marks a value that changes over a unit's life: it rides on the passport's separately signed dynamic surface rather than in a signed snapshot.

post.description:
Subscribes an https endpoint to the versioned passport events of the workspace, all of them or the `eventTypes` named, for every passport or the `resourceScopeDppCodes` named. The answer carries the signing `secret` once; store it, every delivery is signed with it.

A consumer holds at most ten subscriptions and the workspace fifty. Send a test delivery with `POST /webhooks/{id}/test` to see what the endpoint answers before relying on it.

post.description:
